question: A semi-conscious patient with a gag reflex requires airway support after a seizure. She has no head trauma. Which airway adjunct is most appropriate?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: An OPA is contraindicated in patients with an intact gag reflex — it will trigger vomiting and laryngospasm. It is only used in unconscious patients without a gag reflex.

Correct. The NPA is better tolerated in patients with a partially preserved gag reflex because it passes through the nasal route without triggering the oral gag reflex. It is the adjunct of choice in semi-conscious patients.
Endotracheal intubation is an advanced airway technique requiring anaesthesia or sedation and is not indicated as a first-line measure in a semi-conscious patient requiring basic airway support.

answers.text: No adjunct — position the patient in the left lateral decubitus (recovery) position only

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: While recovery position is important, an NPA should be added in a semi-conscious patient who requires maintained airway patency beyond simple positioning.

overallFeedback.feedback: The gag reflex is the key decision gate. OPA requires NO gag reflex; NPA is tolerated even with a partial gag reflex. Review the adjunct selection section.
Correct. The NPA is the adjunct of choice when the gag reflex is present. Remember: OPA = no gag reflex; NPA = gag reflex present or semi-conscious.
